title: Phoenix Exercises
description: Read each example in its lesson first. Predict the result, then check your answer. The notes explain the idea and one common mistake.

exercises.code:
# lib/school_web/router.ex
defmodule SchoolWeb.Router do
 use SchoolWeb, :router
 pipeline :api do
  plug :accepts, ["json"]
 end
 scope "/", SchoolWeb do
  pipe_through :api
get "/hello", LessonController, :hello
 end
end

# lib/school_web/controllers/lesson_controller.ex
defmodule SchoolWeb.LessonController do
 use SchoolWeb, :controller
def hello(conn, _params), do: text(conn, "Hello, Asha!")
end
exercises.question: The router maps GET /hello to a controller action. text sends a plain response. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The router names the controller action. text sends the greeting through the connection value. The SchoolWeb module prefix must match the app name school.

# lib/school_web/controllers/lesson_controller.ex
defmodule SchoolWeb.LessonController do
 use SchoolWeb, :controller
def book(conn, _params), do: json(conn, %{title: "Moon Trip"})
end
exercises.question: json turns an Elixir map into a JSON reply. Open GET /book. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: json turns the atom-keyed map into a JSON object. A map holds named data; its field order is not important.

# lib/school_web/controllers/lesson_controller.ex
defmodule SchoolWeb.LessonController do
 use SchoolWeb, :controller
def hello(conn, %{"name" => name}), do: text(conn, "Hi, #{name}!")
end
exercises.question: A colon marks a router input. Pattern matching reads its string-keyed parameter. Open GET /hello/Ravi. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The pattern reads the string key name from params. It binds Ravi for interpolation. HTTP parameter keys are strings, not atoms.

defmodule SchoolWeb.LessonController do
 use SchoolWeb, :controller
def search(conn, params), do: json(conn, %{term: Map.get(params, "q", "")})
end
exercises.question: The params map includes query values. Open GET /search?q=cat. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Map.get finds q in the parameter map and returns cat. Query values are untrusted text.

exercises.code:
# lib/school_web/router.ex
defmodule SchoolWeb.Router do
 use SchoolWeb, :router
 pipeline :api do
  plug :accepts, ["json"]
 end
 scope "/", SchoolWeb do
  pipe_through :api
get "/double/:n", LessonController, :twice
 end
end

# lib/school_web/controllers/lesson_controller.ex
defmodule SchoolWeb.LessonController do
 use SchoolWeb, :controller
def twice(conn, %{"n" => raw}) do
 case Integer.parse(raw) do
  {n, ""} -> json(conn, %{answer: n * 2})
  _ -> conn |> put_status(400) |> json(%{error: "Use a whole number"})
 end
end
end
exercises.question: Integer.parse reads a number and the unused text. Open GET /double/4. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: Integer.parse returns both 4 and an empty remainder. That exact pattern accepts the input. Check that no trailing text remains after the parsed number.

# lib/school_web/router.ex
defmodule SchoolWeb.Router do
 use SchoolWeb, :router
 pipeline :api do
  plug :accepts, ["json"]
 end
 scope "/", SchoolWeb do
  pipe_through :api
post "/books", LessonController, :create
 end
end

# lib/school_web/controllers/lesson_controller.ex
defmodule SchoolWeb.LessonController do
 use SchoolWeb, :controller
def create(conn, %{"title" => title}) when is_binary(title), do: conn |> put_status(201) |> json(%{title: title})
def create(conn, _params), do: conn |> put_status(400) |> json(%{error: "Title needed"})
end
exercises.question: Send POST /books with application/json and {"title":"Moon Trip"}. The endpoint parser puts the fields into params. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The title pattern and is_binary guard match. The pipe sets 201 before sending JSON. Provide a fallback function clause for input that does not match.

# lib/school_web/controllers/lesson_controller.ex
defmodule SchoolWeb.LessonController do
 use SchoolWeb, :controller
def missing(conn, _params), do: conn |> put_status(404) |> json(%{error: "Book not found"})
end
exercises.question: put_status returns an updated connection. Pass that value to json. Open GET /missing. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: put_status returns a changed connection. The next piped call sends its error map. Connection functions return a new value; keep using that returned value.

defmodule SchoolWeb.LessonController do
 use SchoolWeb, :controller
def note(conn, _params), do: conn |> put_resp_header("cache-control", "no-store") |> text("Practice note")
end
exercises.question: put_resp_header adds a header to the connection. Open GET /note. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: The header call returns a changed connection that text uses for the final reply. Use lower-case header names with Plug.

exercises.code:
# lib/school_web/router.ex
defmodule SchoolWeb.Router do
 use SchoolWeb, :router
 pipeline :api do
  plug :accepts, ["json"]
 end
 scope "/", SchoolWeb do
  pipe_through :api
get "/start", LessonController, :start
get "/hello", LessonController, :hello
 end
end

# lib/school_web/controllers/lesson_controller.ex
defmodule SchoolWeb.LessonController do
 use SchoolWeb, :controller
def start(conn, _params), do: redirect(conn, to: "/hello")
def hello(conn, _params), do: text(conn, "Welcome")
end
exercises.question: redirect sends a location. A browser following GET /start reaches /hello. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: redirect sets an internal location. The browser follows it to the hello action. Use an internal path for this example, not an unchecked outside destination.

# lib/school_web/controllers/lesson_controller.ex
defmodule SchoolWeb.LessonController do
 use SchoolWeb, :controller
def closed(conn, _params), do: conn |> send_resp(403, "Closed for practice") |> halt()
end
exercises.question: halt marks the connection so later plugs stop. Open GET /closed. What result does this example give after the setup steps?
exercises.explanation: send_resp writes the 403 body. halt then marks the connection to stop later plugs. halt does not itself send a response; send it first.
